To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sympathectomy does not change the histone localization, but decreases the template activity of chromosomal DNA, and the proportion of epinephrine-containing neurons in LC.
the guanethidine-induced sympathectomy of the rat causes a significant reduction of the epinephrine content in the LC neurons and a decrease in the template activity of their nuclei and chromatin.
the guanethidine induced sympathectomy in rat leads to a decrease in the epinephrine content and template activity in the neurons of the locus coeruleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the sympathetic innervation is essential for the normal development of LC cells.
the question whether the LC neurons are capable of changing their transcription activity in the course of GS.
the question: whether sympathectomy causes the decrease in the transcriptional activity of LC neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LC cells are not only the locus coeruleus neurons but they are a group of cells with different transcription levels.
GS causes the decrease in the number of LC cells in active stage and the increase in number of inactive ones.
guanethidine-induced sympathectomy causes changes in the epinephrine metabolism of LC cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
guanethidine-induced sympathectomy causes the decrease in the number of LC neurons with high template activity.
guanethidine treatment of the rat pups during the first 14 days of life leads to the decrease of LC cell epinephrine content and to the decrease in the proportion of cells with active chromatin.
GS is not a factor of the chromatin reprogramming in LC neurons, but the decrease in epinephrinic fluorescence is connected with the inhibition of the transcriptional activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LC cells are not a uniform population and the sympathectomy affects their transcriptional activity.
GS causes the decrease in epinephrin fluorescence and in template activity of the LC neurons.
LC cell classes can be defined by their template activity.
